h: Old Stones, Fresh Food and the Fylde on Your Doorstep
p: Poulton's market has a proper sense of history about it. The Market Place has been at the centre of town life for centuries, and it still holds a few relics of the past, including the old stocks, the market cross and the fish stones where traders once laid out their catch. It's well worth a few minutes to look around while you browse the stalls.

A good market morning in Poulton goes something like this: arrive fairly early for the best choice, have a slow wander round all the stalls before you buy anything, then grab a brew in one of the nearby cafés while you decide what you really need. Traders are usually happy to chat, so ask what's good this week. If you're driving, the town has car parks within easy walking distance of the centre, and Poulton station has trains to Blackpool and Preston.
Monday mornings can be busy with locals, so bring a bit of patience and a good bag for your shopping. It's an easy-going market that suits a gentle wander rather than a rushed dash.

The wider Fylde has lots to pair with a visit. Marsh Mill in Thornton is a handsome old windmill that's a real local landmark, and Fleetwood, with its market, tram links and seafront, is just up the coast. Lytham's elegant green and windmill are a lovely contrast to Blackpool's bright lights, and the Wyre Estuary Country Park offers peaceful walks by the water. Mix and match and you've got a proper Fylde day out.
